newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE COCOA FOLLOWS NY DOWN IN THIN TRADE.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE COCOA FOLLOWS NY DOWN IN THIN TRADE.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa followed New York down in low volume in the morning session.
September last traded eight stg lower at 1,027 stg after opening 11 stg down on Tuesday's close of 1,035. December last traded at 1,056 stg, down nine.
"New York was very disappointing," a trader said. "There was a lot of speculative buying and then origin selling came in and pushed it back down and London is following suit."
Traders said uncertainty about currency movements after sterling's recent fall was deterring the market and kept volume low in the morning session.
March had the biggest volume with 293 lots out of a total 1,133, followed by December with 280 lots.
"With currency running around the way it is it's deterring people in London. That's what's keeping the volume so low," a trader said.
Sterling was ticking lower against the mark and dollar at the European mid-session, pressured partly by indications from the Bank of England that a pause in UK monetary policy should now be possible.
Technical analysts said support for London's September contract appeared fairly solid at 1,010 stg.
"Support is mainly at 1,010 and it's unlikely to be tested," said Elli Gifford, an independent technical analyst.
